description: Map Studio component properties. The list is closed: later versions add properties here and in docs/.

startingArea.description: Where this component opens the map (epic 3 entry 6, docs/contract.md): a centre and zoom, or bounds. When all four bounds are numbers with west < east and south < north, the map fits them; otherwise it opens on the centre at the zoom. Two components on one page may open on different areas; both show the same map items. An invalid value opens on the whole world.

center.description: The centre of the starting view, WGS 84.

bounds.description: Bounds to fit instead of the centre and zoom, WGS 84; leave any value null to use the centre and zoom.

previewStyles.description: Draw the style preview panel over the map (epic 3 entry 1, docs/styles.md): every kind's style rule and area tints, each case in its preset, and the preset and tint palettes. The kind setup screen's preview, shown here for review; off by default.

editMode.description: Edit mode, both ways (epic 4 entry 2, docs/contract.md). True opens the studio for a session with the full editing role; the Edit switch on the map writes the value back, so a binding follows the mode, and a value the page writes after the component mounted enters or leaves Edit mode. A session without the full editing role stays in View mode and the value is left as written. Off by default.

selectedItem.description: The selected map item's id, both ways (epic 4 entries 2 and 14, docs/contract.md): the component writes it on every selection change (a marker click, a list row, a search or Needs you choice; a tap on the ground clears it to null), and an id the page writes selects that item as a click on it does (in View mode centred or fitted with its popup, in Edit mode with Details open); null clears the selection, and an id not on the map clears it with one console warning. The component's own write coming back is ignored. Read it from a binding or the onItemSelected event.

viewport.description: Read-only (output). Where the map is looking (epic 4 entry 14, docs/contract.md), written by the component when the map first settles and then once its moves settle (200 ms after the last move end), never during a move or once per frame: {center: [lng, lat], zoom, bounds: [[west, south], [east, north]]}, WGS 84 to 6 decimals, the zoom to 2. The onViewportChanged event carries the same object. A value the page writes is not read, and the next move that changes the view writes it again; null until the map has settled.

center.description: The map's centre, [lng, lat], WGS 84, to 6 decimals.

zoom.description: The zoom, 0 (the world) to 24, to 2 decimals.

bounds.description: The visible bounds, [[west, south], [east, north]], WGS 84, to 6 decimals.

userLocation.description: The device's position for the you-are-here marker and Locate me (epic 4 entry 15, docs/contract.md). Bind it in one binding to {session.props.geolocation}, whose shape it takes: {enabled, permissionGranted, options, data: {latitude, longitude, accuracy, altitude, heading, speed, timestamp}}; every key is optional and extra keys are ignored. A position is known when enabled and permissionGranted are true and data holds a latitude from -90 to 90 and a longitude from -180 to 180: the marker is drawn there (the accuracy in metres as a circle, the heading as a wedge) and Locate me centres the map on it. Otherwise Locate me is off and says why. The component reads nothing of the session and asks the browser for nothing. Null (unbound) by default.

enabled.description: Whether the session's location is on (session.props.geolocation.enabled).

permissionGranted.description: Whether the browser granted location permission (session.props.geolocation.permissionGranted).

options.description: The session's location options, not read by the component.

accuracy.description: The fix's accuracy in metres, drawn as a circle on the ground; none when missing or not positive.

altitude.description: Altitude in metres, not read by the component.

heading.description: Heading in degrees clockwise from north, drawn as a wedge from the dot when it is a number.

speed.description: Speed in metres per second, not read by the component.

timestamp.description: When the fix was taken, not read by the component.
